title: Pikachu's space trip connects Pokémon with a science exhibition
summary:
A Pikachu plush has returned from an adventure far beyond the Pokémon world. The European Space Agency, known as ESA, revealed on September 19, 2026, that the toy had spent 67 days aboard the International Space Station.

Pikachu launched on a Cygnus cargo spacecraft on April 11 and returned to Earth on a SpaceX Dragon cargo spacecraft on June 17. Cargo spacecraft carry supplies and other items. During its time in orbit, the plush completed about 1,040 journeys around Earth. An orbit is the path an object follows around another object in space.

The project was timed to help launch World Space Week 2026, which runs from October 4 to 10. ESA has created an exhibition that combines Pokémon characters with information about actual space exploration.

The displays introduce European space missions and life aboard the station. Visitors can also explore how ESA studies the Sun, the Solar System and the wider universe.

The exhibition tour began at ESA's headquarters in Paris, France, in late September. It is planned to travel to museums and other venues across Europe through April 2027.

There is also a Pokémon GO connection. From October 4, 2026, to April 30, 2027, players visiting participating European science and space museums will be able to join special game activities. These include One-Star Raids featuring Astronaut Pikachu, research tasks and opportunities to encounter event-themed Pokémon.

ESA hopes the project will spark curiosity about space and science among children and teenagers. Director General Josef Aschbacher said inspiring future generations is a key part of the agency's mission.
why_it_matters: The exhibition uses Pokémon characters to introduce real space exploration. Its displays offer information about space missions and the universe, while ESA hopes the project will interest young people in science.
